And after that, throught out the whole meal, no one came to provide us any answer nor apologized, 
When we asked for the bill after finished eating. Another waiter who didn’t serve us came with the check, still no explanation nor apology were said. So we asked about it. The waiter nonchalantly answered, saying it was a bill. That’s all! 
We were shocked with how they dealt with it. We asked them to report it to the manager or anyone could be responsible for it. They said the manager took a day off today. And still no apology!
Only after we brought the apology matter up and made a fuss about it, they simply said sorry half-heartedly! Asked a human being, and especially a customer, I felt really offended and taken a back at how can someone can be lack of simple manner.
In the end no manager or supervisor showed up to take responsibility! One of the waitress and the cashier had really bad attitude!

2nd visit to Cha Ca La Vong
Nov 2015 • Business
This is the second time I've visited this restaurant for lunch as the guest of a long time customer. Only one dish is served, after which the restaurant is named, which was originated in Ha Noi. At the restaurant in Ha Noi where it reputedly was invented and is still served by the fifth generation the fish is brought to the table on a sizzling hot griddle. At this restaurant it is brought to the table in a bowl set atop a gas burner. I prefer the latter because it is less oily and has more marinade. What really makes it special is the very strong fresh anchovy paste. The fish portions do seem to have gotten smaller from first to second visit.

Turmeric gold
Jan 2015 • Family
This dish of fried catfish marinated in turmeric was 'invented' in Hà Nội in the 19th century by the same family that still owns Lã Vọng. Compared to the original version, the two outlets in Sài Gòn have made several concessions to Southern taste - less oil to fry the fish, and no cà cuống (essence of a water bug eaten in many SE Asian countries). Nowadays, you can find better renditions at other restaurants, especially in Hà Nội. The food is still very good. Portions are tiny, so you should count on ordering more than one portion per person (there is only one item being served).

Fresh and flavorful!
Apr 2013 • Friends
My Vietnamese landlord took me here for my birthday and it was UH-mazing. I often avoid fish in Vietnamese restaurants because I spend most of my time picking out bones, but these chunks were huge, succulent and bone-free, The outside gets caramelized over the burner and the green onions and dill are sauteed in just enough time to turn them bright green and slightly wilted. Break up a rice cracker into the bottom of your bowl, plop in bun noodles, pile on the fish & greens, drop in a sprig of cilantro if you like, sprinkle peanuts, and drizzle fish and/or shrimp sauce. It is a masterpiece. The service was attentive, restaurant was clean, and clientele all locals. The atmosphere is totally adequate, but you're not coming here for decor. It's all about the fish!
